subject: Operator safeguards and rollback guarantees — MSA addendum review
messages:
From: Sarah Blake <sarah.blake@crestwave.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@crestwave.com>; Maya Rao <maya.rao@crestwave.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: operator safeguards + rollback guarantees (MSA addendum)

Alex — thanks again for the demo on Tuesday. As we move this through legal & procurement, two items surfaced that the board and our security team want clarified in the MSA / Order Form addendum for on-prem (private) hosting: 

1) Operator access boundaries: explicit language on who may perform operator actions, scope of their access (console, snapshots, keys) and a witnessing requirement for any offload/transfer.
2) Rollback / exit guarantee: we want contractual commitments for an orderly rollback (runbook, timeline, data egress, and a third-party witness or escrow-lite option if operator access is required to effect the rollback).

Attached is our preferred redline (Doc: Draft_MSA_Addendum_v2_redlines.docx) with comment bubbles. Can you confirm Redwood's position on: whether you can accept a witness-based snapshot delivery to a neutral custodian (attested handover) instead of full code escrow, and whether you can sign to a committed runbook SLA for rollback timelines?

We have a procurement deadline the week of Nov 8 — ideally we lock language this week.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Blake
Sr. Director, Security & Compliance
Crestwave Health

--
Attachment: Draft_MSA_Addendum_v2_redlines.docx (MS Word redline, ~45KB)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Blake <sarah.blake@crestwave.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 10:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operator safeguards + rollback guarantees (MSA addendum)

Sarah — appreciate the clear redlines and timeline. Quick reply while we thread internal legal:

- Short answer: we can work toward a witnessing-based custody path rather than traditional code escrow in many cases. Our standard approach for private deployments is a staged evidence handover: encrypted snapshots + signed attestations + third-party custodian hold.

- Rollback/runbook SLA: we can commit to providing a certified rollback runbook and a runbook witness session (remote witness + signed witness log). We can discuss timeline SLAs in the Order Form exhibit — we typically offer an operational window (e.g., 48-72 hours for confirmed rollback support) but will confirm with Ops & Legal if Crestwave needs a tighter SLA.

I've looped in Lauren (Legal) and Irene (Ops/Governance) to pull precise proposed language and a minimal evidence checklist. We'll review your redline and propose counter-language by COB Mon (Nov 1).

Attachments: I will upload a baseline Runbook_Template_v1.pdf that shows how we structure witnessing and attestations.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: Runbook_Template_v1.pdf (PDF, runbook skeleton)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Blake <sarah.blake@crestwave.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operator safeguards + rollback guarantees (MSA addendum)

Sarah — thanks for the redline. I reviewed the document and left inline comments on three key topics:

1) "Operator Access" definition: we can accept a narrower definition that limits operator actions to a defined list (snapshot creation, read-only filesystem export, and restart actions) so long as Crestwave retains control of keys for production data. We will propose explicit ACL language in the MSA exhibit.

2) Witnessing vs Escrow: Redwood is open to an "escrow-lite" model: a) periodic encrypted snapshot deposits to a neutral custodian, b) mutual attestation (signed by Redwood Ops lead + Crestwave security rep) upon any transfer, c) limited-time access tokens issued only for the handover window. This reduces need for full source code escrow while providing verifiable evidence of custody.

3) Rollback/runbook SLA: we will propose a Runbook Exhibit that includes:
   - Certified runbook delivery within 7 business days of order effective date (for staging/testing)
   - For an actual rollback event, Redwood will initiate rollback support within 24 hours of validated request and provide a best-effort completion target with regular status updates.

Open items for Crestwave to confirm: whether Crestwave requires (i) a binding monetary remedy if rollback extends past a specified window and (ii) a neutral third-party custodian candidate or whether Redwood may propose one.

If those two items are firm, we can convert language into redline-ready MSA/Order Form text and route to procurement for signature.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
--
Note: see inline comments in Draft_MSA_Addendum_v2_redlines.docx (uploaded to Drive)

From: Sarah Blake <sarah.blake@crestwave.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@crestwave.com>, Maya Rao <maya.rao@crestwave.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operator safeguards + rollback guarantees (MSA addendum)

Thanks Lauren — that approach is promising and maps close to what the board will accept. A few responses inline: 

- Operator Access: we agree to the narrower action set but Crestwave must retain exclusive control of the production KMS keys (we will add a sentence to the redline clarifying key custody).
- Escrow-lite: Crestwave prefers Redwood to propose a neutral custodian (you can propose two options). We would like monthly snapshot cadence for the first 3 months post-go-live, then quarterly for the rest of the term.
- Rollback SLA: our security council will accept the 24-hour initiation but will request a financial remedy if the supported rollback is not completed within a mutually-agreed period (we can live with a 5-business-day completion window for full data recovery; remedies to be modest but meaningful).

Procurement note: Maya, we'll need a final redline and an order-form with committed runbook exhibit by Nov 8 to meet our procurement window.

Sarah

--

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Blake <sarah.blake@crestwave.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operator safeguards + rollback guarantees (MSA addendum)

Sarah — quick operational confirmation from my side:

1) Neutral custodian proposals: we can propose two well-known custodians (Lockbox Partners LLC and CustodyOne). Both support encrypted snapshot holds and attestation logs.
2) Snapshot cadence: monthly for first 90 days, then quarterly — agreed and operationally feasible. We will include a retention and rotation schedule in the Runbook Exhibit.
3) Witnessing model: Redwood Ops will perform a live remote witness session with Crestwave security during any transfer and produce a signed witnessing log (time-stamped, hash of snapshot, list of personnel present).

Next step: Lauren — if you can confirm accept/reject on the monetary remedy clause, I will draft redline language for the Runbook Exhibit and the third-party custodian clause and send a consolidated redline by EOD Nov 2. Alex — I will need the Ops lead signature block to add to the attestation template.

Irene Choi
Director, Operations Governance
Redwood Inference
